contract.close_semantics: closeMainWindow -> NSWindow.performClose (AppDelegate.swift:5702-5709). windowShouldClose = handleMainTerminalWindowShouldClose (:16232-16239): returns true (close proceeds) under XCTest, while terminating, or when >1 main windows exist; for the LAST window it invokes handleQuitShortcutWarning and returns FALSE (close vetoed). handleQuitShortcutWarning (:12831-12856): if quit confirmation not required -> NSApp.terminate immediately; else presents async quit-confirmation alert, terminating only on confirm. entries.server_side: window.display: invalid_params `Missing or invalid display` when display param absent; explicit window_id branch -> success {display, window_id, window_ref, moved:[id]} or not_found `Window not found` (data {window_id, window_ref}) when the window is missing, else not_found `Display not found: <query>` with data {requested, available:[names]}; all-windows branch -> {display, moved:[ids]} or the same display-not-found error (ControlCommandCoordinator+Window.swift:191-238).
adversarial: canonical_cli.json lists --workspace and --json as significant flags for `window`; --workspace has NO parse site in runWindowNamespace/display paths at the pinned commit (extraction noise) - only --json, --window (global), --list/-l, --clear are real.

Window-not-found vs display-not-found error order in window.display: window existence is checked only AFTER the move fails (controlMoveWindow nil -> check controlWindowExists) (ControlCommandCoordinator+Window.swift:198-215).
Display name matching is a server-side query string; the CLI passes it verbatim (quoted names with spaces).

entries.usage: cmux surface resume set [flags] -- <argv...> | cmux surface resume set [flags] --shell <command> | cmux surface resume show|get [--json] [flags] | cmux surface resume clear [flags]  (also invocable as `cmux surface-resume <sub> ...`)
entries.subcommands: first arg lowercased; DEFAULT is `show` when no args (CLI/cmux.swift:6570). set / show / get (alias of show) / clear; anything else -> CLIError `Unsupported surface resume subcommand: <sub>` (:6659-6660).

flags.target (all subcommands): --workspace, --surface, --window (surfaceResumeTargetValueOptions, CLI/cmux.swift:6730). --window falls back to the GLOBAL --window override (:6786).
flags.set: --name, --kind, --checkpoint, --checkpoint-id (takes precedence), --source (default 'cli'), --cwd (default $PWD env else FileManager cwd), --shell <command>, or `-- <argv...>` terminator (:6580-6617).
flags.note: canonical_cli.json lists `-t` and `--session` for surface-resume; NO parse site exists in runSurfaceResumeCommand/surfaceResumeTarget at the pinned commit (those flags belong to tmux-compat/vm commands, CLI/cmux.swift:22689,11432) - extraction noise, do not implement.

entries.target_resolution: surfaceResumeTarget (CLI/cmux.swift:6773-6808): parses --workspace/--surface/--window before `--`; ambient env defaults: CMUX_SURFACE_ID used when no --surface/--workspace/--window given; CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID used only when no --surface, no implicit surface, and no window; explicit --window (or global override) suppresses ambient env. Handles normalized via normalizeWindowHandle/normalizeWorkspaceHandle/normalizeSurfaceHandle (client-side ref/index resolution) into params window_id/workspace_id/surface_id.
entries.pre_socket_validation: validateSurfaceResumeValueOptions runs BEFORE any socket call: every recognized value option must be followed by a value that is not `--`, not another option name, and not blank -> CLIError `surface resume <sub>: <flag> requires a value` (:6737-6759). set additionally pre-validates the --shell/argv token contract (:6712-6728).
entries.set_command_construction: --shell wins: any leftover token (before or after --) -> CLIError `surface resume set: unexpected argument '<tok>' after --shell. Quote the full shell command or use -- <argv...>`; command = trimmed shell string. Without --shell: tokens after `--` (or remaining tokens) become argv, each single-quoted via cliShellQuote (`'` -> `'\''`, CLI/cmux.swift:6810-6812) and space-joined; argv present + stray pre-`--` token -> `unexpected argument '<tok>' before --`; empty -> `surface resume set requires --shell <command> or -- <argv...>`; final empty command -> `surface resume set requires a non-empty command` (:6597-6615).
entries.wire: set -> v2 surface.resume.set with params {target ids, name?, kind?, checkpoint_id?, source (always sent, default 'cli'), cwd (always sent), command}; show/get -> surface.resume.get; clear -> surface.resume.clear with optional checkpoint_id/source (CLI/cmux.swift:6618-6657).

output.show/get: --json prints id-formatted payload; else prints the binding command string, or `No resume binding` when resume_binding null/command empty (:6629-6638)

adversarial: Bare `cmux surface-resume` (no subcommand) is `show`, hitting the focused surface via ambient/env resolution.
set ALWAYS sends source (default 'cli') and cwd (default caller $PWD) even when flags are omitted - the server-side approval store keys off source.
argv mode shell-quotes every token: `-- opencode --session x` becomes `'opencode' '--session' 'x'` as the stored command string.
--checkpoint-id silently beats --checkpoint when both given (set and clear).
Explicit --window suppresses BOTH ambient CMUX_SURFACE_ID and CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID (server resolves the window's focused terminal).
entries.windows_gap: classified only (classify.rs:460,569 lists surface-resume; help text via SUBCOMMAND_USAGE). No target-resolution helpers, no argv quoting/`--` contract, no v2 mapping, no output formatting, no backend surface.resume.* to call on either branch.

exact_error_and_payload_reference.purpose: The entry summaries do not authorize approximate strings/shapes. Red tests must transcribe byte-for-byte from these pinned-commit sources.

proposed_red_test_build_scopes.targets: Route window.create/window.close/window.focus, surface.refresh, surface.resume.set/get/clear in control_socket.rs. Red tests in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/control_socket/tests/ (pattern: pane_surface_lifecycle_red.rs on parity/lifecycle-desktop-green): capability advertisement, exact error code/message/order (incl. the two distinct unavailable messages and the minted-ref-in-not_found-data quirk), exact success key sets with explicit nulls, resume target-resolution matrix (surface_id/terminal_id/tab_id aliases, window/workspace scoping, malformed-selector rejection BEFORE routing, global locate), checkpoint/source clear guards with cleared flag semantics, auto_resume agent-hook gate, process-detected->manual rewrite, surface.refresh terminal-only count, window lifecycle event emission (window.created/focused/closed with payload keys), last-window close veto seam (injectable confirmation), focus-intent policy gating (create/close never activate; focus does).

proposed_red_test_build_scopes.scope: cmux-core / session model crates (whatever owns workspace/surface snapshots on windows-port)
proposed_red_test_build_scopes.targets: Authoritative per-window model: window id registry + ref minting, active-window pointer transitions on create/close/key, closed-window history suppression flag, session snapshot save-on-window-close (no scrollback) vs termination path, per-surface resume-binding storage keyed by terminal surface with persistence round-trip and non-terminal rejection (Workspace.swift:4719-4738 parity), approval-store state machine (stored approval application, promptless CLI-manual, prompt bypass under tests).

Parser/mapping/help/formatter tests plus real named-pipe process-contract tests: new-window (v1 `new_window`, raw `OK <uuid>` passthrough, --json ignored), focus-window/close-window (--window required, per-command flag NOT global override, client-side normalizeWindowHandle UUID/ref/index resolution against window.list with exact error strings), window namespace (subcommand hints incl. the default-display omission quirk, displays/display text formats, default-display pre-socket file path), surface-resume (default-show, value-option pre-socket validation strings, --shell vs `--` argv quoting via cliShellQuote, ambient CMUX_SURFACE_ID/CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID suppression rules, always-sent source/cwd, show `No resume binding` output, byte-frozen help).

dependencies_on_existing_code: Shared routing selectors + uuid/ref helpers already specified and partially built for the pane_surface_lifecycle batch (ControlRoutingSelectors precedence, handle registry) - window.* and resume reuse them verbatim.

surface.resume rendering in surface.list rows (resume_binding payload) is shared with pane_surface_lifecycle's surface.list contract; the payload builder (surfaceResumeBindingPayload) must be ONE implementation.

window.list/window.current/window.displays/window.display already exist on the Windows desktop socket (both branches) and become regression dependencies: window.create/close/focus mutate the model those reads consume; CLI handle resolution (--window ref/index) calls window.list.

cmux-cli foundation (invocation/socket/classify/dispatch, v1+v2 client codecs in cmux-ipc) exists on windows-port; these five commands need per-command mapping layers on top (v1 line codec for new/focus/close-window, v2 for surface-resume and window display).
risks: window.close success-despite-veto and last-window quit-coupling are easy to get wrong: a naive implementation that closes unconditionally (current window.rs behavior) or errors on last window diverges from canonical.
Focus policy inversion: implementing window.create with activation (natural on Tauri) violates the suppress-by-default socket policy; only window.focus (and v1 focus_window) may take focus.
Resume target resolution has 6 ordered fallback branches including a GLOBAL cross-window locate; collapsing them to 'resolve workspace then surface' breaks the pinned multi-window tests.
The two different unavailable messages ('TabManager not available' vs 'cmux window is not available. Reopen the window and try again.') and validation-before-routing ordering are byte-frozen.
canonical_cli.json extraction noise (-t/--session on surface-resume, --workspace on window) must not be implemented; the Swift parse sites are the truth.

headless_impossibility_flags.item: OS key-window activation / app foregrounding for window.focus (makeKeyAndOrderFront + NSRunningApplication.activate equivalent)
headless_impossibility_flags.rationale: Win32 foreground rules (SetForegroundWindow lock) differ from macOS activation; headless CI cannot observe real key-window transfer. Contract-test the seam (focus request recorded, window.focused event emitted, active-window pointer moved) and mark the real foregrounding as platform_equivalent verified via hosted live differential only.

headless_impossibility_flags.item: Quit-confirmation NSAlert on last-window close and the blocking resume-approval NSAlert
headless_impossibility_flags.rationale: Canonical itself bypasses both under XCTest (AppDelegate.swift:16234-16235; SurfaceResumeApprovalStore isRunningTests, TerminalController+ControlSurfaceContext4.swift:104-110). Windows red tests must inject a confirmation handler seam (canonical precedent: debugCloseMainWindowConfirmationHandler, AppDelegate.swift:5718-5723) rather than drive real dialogs.

headless_impossibility_flags.item: surface.refresh actual renderer redraw (forceRefresh of the terminal surface)
headless_impossibility_flags.rationale: The wire contract (routing, terminal-only count, payload) is fully headless; the visual refresh maps to the xterm.js renderer refresh on Windows and is only observable in the live app.
Already-routed reads; frame/display enumeration needs real monitors. In scope here only as the cli:window mapping target; live differential required for promotion.
